description: Password login. Browser posts JSON credentials; the Node server converts them to HTTP Basic and forwards to the cluster proxy's /login. Relays the proxy's Set-Cookie and additionally duplicates YTCypressCookie under the per-cluster name <cluster>_YTCypressCookie. Route is flagged ui:true so an auth failure never turns into a 401 redirect.

request.body: {"username": "admin", "password": "secret"} - raw Buffer, body parsers are disabled for /api/yt/* (configs/common.ts:13-41), handler does JSON.parse(req.body)

response.body_schema: empty body on success (the proxy replies with no payload). On failure the proxy's YT-error JSON body is piped through: {code:int, message:string, attributes:object, inner_errors:array}. The UI server maps proxy 401 -> 400 at login.ts:80-83 before pipeAxiosErrorOrFalse streams the response with that rewritten status.

description: Changes the current user's YT password. SHA-256s both passwords server-side, fetches login+csrf_token from the proxy's /auth/whoami, then calls the v4 driver command set_user_password with X-Csrf-Token.

response.body_schema: {"result": <driver result, empty for set_user_password>}; errors: {message:string} or YT error JSON with status 500

cookies: <ytAuthCluster>_YTCypressCookie (read to build the upstream Cookie header)

description: Logout. If OAuth is configured and the user has OAuth cookies, redirects to the IdP logout URL; otherwise (when allowPasswordAuth is on) deletes YTCypressCookie and every <cluster>_YTCypressCookie, then redirects to /. The cluster-side session is NOT revoked - the proxy has no /logout endpoint.

response.body_schema: empty (redirect)

description: The endpoint through which the browser learns who it is and gets the CSRF token. Server-side it runs GET <proxy>/auth/whoami and GET <proxy>/version concurrently (Promise.allSettled). The client stores token.csrf_token in the JS cookie ytfront_<cluster>_xsrf_token and sets global.login from token.login. A missing csrf_token or a tokenError makes the client render PRELOAD_ERROR.AUTHENTICATION and refuse the cluster page.

response.body_schema: {token?: {login: string, csrf_token: string, realm?: string, real_login?: string}, version?: string, tokenError?: {message,code,inner_errors}, versionError?: {message,code,inner_errors}}

description: Per-cluster authorization badge for the clusters menu. Pure cookie-presence check with no upstream call. When allowPasswordAuth is off every cluster is hard-coded to authorized:true.

response.body_schema: {"<clusterId>": {"authorized": boolean}, ...}

description: Starts the OIDC authorization-code flow in the hardened standalone UI checkout (not the stock image used by the parent deployment). Requires a fully configured ytOAuthSettings, including an explicit safe callbackBaseUrl. Sets one fixed __Host-yt_oauth_state cookie containing {state, retPath} for 10 minutes and redirects to new URL(authPath, baseURL).

response.body_schema: empty (redirect)

description: OIDC redirect target in the hardened standalone UI checkout. Requires exactly one raw __Host-yt_oauth_state cookie and a constant-time match with the required state query value, consumes the cookie before exchanging code via POST new URL(tokenPath, baseURL), stores tokens in __Host- cookies, and redirects only to the validated local retPath.

params.state: state_<uuid> (query, required and matched in constant time)

Set-Cookie: __Host-yt_oauth_refresh_token=<token>; Max-Age=<refresh_expires_in>; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax (only when returned)

response.body_schema: empty on 302 redirect; invalid/missing state or code -> generic 400 text; token-exchange failure -> generic 502 text with no IdP error details

description: Post-logout redirect target for the IdP. Clears both OAuth cookies and redirects to /.

response.body_schema: empty (redirect)

description: Generic authenticated pass-through to the cluster proxy's /api/<version>/<command>. Strips the browser's host/cookie/X-Custom-Request-Id headers, forwards everything else (including X-Csrf-Token), and injects the credential header built by the auth middleware (Cookie: YTCypressCookie=<secret> or Cookie: access_token=<oauth>, or nothing when the cluster's authentication is 'none'). Adds X-YT-Correlation-Id and X-YT-Suppress-Redirect: 1. Heavy commands are first routed via GET <proxy>/hosts.

headers.X-Csrf-Token: <csrf_token> - set by Axios and forwarded verbatim only when cluster authentication is not 'none'
headers.X-Custom-Request-Id: optional, consumed by the UI server for stats and NOT forwarded

params.command: driver command name, validated against the javascript-wrapper command table + {get_job_stderr,get_job_input,get_job_fail_context}

response.body_schema: streamed proxy response verbatim; on auth failure the UI server answers 401 {message:string} before ever contacting the proxy

description: Whitelisted pass-through to two non-/api proxy routes, with the user's credential header attached. command must be 'hosts-all' (-> /hosts/all) or 'internal-discover_versions' (-> /internal/discover_versions/v2).

response.body_schema: streamed proxy response verbatim; unknown command -> 500 {message:'Error: Unexpected action <cmd>'}

description: Preloaded cluster parameters. Uses the ROBOT credentials (Authorization: OAuth <ytInterfaceSecret.oauthToken or $YT_TOKEN>) or none when the cluster's authentication is 'none'. Issues a v3 execute_batch for //sys/media, //sys/scheduler/orchid/service/version, //sys/@ui_config, //sys/@ui_config_dev_overrides and the primary master version.

response.body_schema: {mediumList, schedulerVersion, masterVersion, uiConfig, uiDevConfig}

description: Fetches GET <proxy>/version for every configured cluster. No credentials are attached.

response.body_schema: [{id: string, version?: string}]

description: Remote user settings stored in Cypress. Uses the ROBOT credentials, not the user's. Inactive unless userSettingsConfig is set in the UI config; the client then falls back to localStorage.

response.body_schema: settings document or the driver result; errors as {message} / YT error JSON

description: Health check. The only route with authPolicy: AuthPolicy.disabled, i.e. it never runs the auth middleware.

response.body_schema: {"result": "pong"}

description: HTML entry points (ui:true). The rendered page inlines window.YT.parameters = {interface:{version}, login, authWay} and a __DATA__ JSON blob with allowPasswordAuth/allowOAuth/oauthButtonLabel. login comes from req.yt.login which the auth middleware filled from the proxy's /auth/whoami; in local-cluster mode it is hard-coded to 'root'. authWay is 'oauth' | 'passwd' | undefined. The client shows the login form iff allowPasswordAuth && (!login || showLoginDialog) (plus a ytAuthCluster requirement when authWay is set).

response.body_schema: HTML with <script>window.YT = {...,{parameters:{interface:{version},login,authWay}}}</script> and <script id="__DATA__">{allowPasswordAuth, allowOAuth, oauthButtonLabel, ytApiUseCORS, uiSettings, settings, ...}</script>

description: Cypress cookie login. Registered only when auth/cypress_cookie_manager is configured, and deliberately NOT wrapped in CORS. Accepts any HTTP method and branches purely on the presence of the Authorization header. Verifies sha256_hex(salt + sha256_hex(password)) against //sys/users/<user>/@hashed_password, then stores a session at //sys/cypress_cookies/<value>.

request.body: none - no JSON body is ever parsed

headers.Set-Cookie: YTCypressCookie=<64 hex chars>; Expires=<RFC822>; Secure; HttpOnly; [Domain=<d>; ]Path=/ (Secure and HttpOnly default true; Domain only if configured; NO SameSite ever)
headers.Location: <redirect_url> only when cookie_generator/redirect_url is set, together with status 301

response.body_schema: empty on success. Missing Authorization -> 401 + 'WWW-Authenticate: Basic', empty body. Malformed header -> 400 with YT error JSON. Wrong credentials -> 401 + 'WWW-Authenticate: Basic' + {"code":1,"message":"Incorrect login or password","attributes":{...},"inner_errors":[]}

description: The identity + CSRF-token endpoint. Authenticates with disableCsrfTokenCheck=true, so no X-Csrf-Token is required. This is the single gate the UI Node server uses to decide whether a session is valid; the UI reads only 'login' and 'csrf_token' from the response.

headers.Authorization: OAuth <token> | Bearer <token> - alternative to the cookie
headers.X-YT-Correlation-Id: <requestId>.getXSRFToken - set by the UI server, purely for tracing

headers.Cache-Control: max-age=0, must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate, no-cache, no-store, private

response.body_schema: {"login": string, "realm": string, "real_login": string, "csrf_token": string}. csrf_token = hex(hmac_sha256(csrf_secret, "<login>:<unixtime>")) + ":" + <unixtime>. On failure: 401 for InvalidCredentials(111)/InvalidCsrfToken(110)/AuthenticationError(900), otherwise 503, with X-YT-Error/X-YT-Response-Code/X-YT-Response-Message headers and a serialized TError JSON body. No WWW-Authenticate.

description: The driver command endpoint (version is v3 or v4, one handler for the whole /api/ subtree). Credential resolution order: (1) if auth/require_authentication is false -> user is 'root' or whatever X-YT-User-Name says, no credential is inspected; (2) Authorization: OAuth|Bearer <token>; (3) Cookie (YTCypressCookie / Session_id / sessionid2 / sessguard / access_token / yc_session) - and for non-GET methods an X-Csrf-Token header is REQUIRED and validated; (4) X-Ya-User-Ticket; (5) X-Ya-Service-Ticket; otherwise InvalidCredentials 'Client is missing credentials'. Bare /api returns ["v3","v4"]; /api/v4/ with an empty command dumps the command descriptors; command names must match [A-Za-z_]+.

headers.X-Csrf-Token: <csrf_token from /auth/whoami> - required only for cookie auth on non-GET
headers.X-YT-User-Name: impersonation (needs superuser/whitelist) or free user selection when authentication is disabled
headers.X-YT-Suppress-Redirect: 1 - set by both the UI server and the javascript-wrapper

headers.X-YT-Error: <compact TError JSON> (on error, or in trailers if the body was already streaming)
headers.Set-Cookie: refreshed YTCypressCookie when within cookie_renewal_period of expiry

response.body_schema: command output. 401 for InvalidCredentials/InvalidCsrfToken/AuthenticationError; 403 'User validation failed' or 'User %Qv is not allowed to access proxy with role %Qv'; 400 for generic command errors (TContext::Finalize forces 400); 503 for any other auth-layer error including 'Malformed CSRF token'.

description: Driver whoami command, registered for both v3 and v4. Returns only the authenticated user name, no CSRF token. NOT used by the YTsaurus UI - the UI uses /auth/whoami instead because that is the only endpoint that mints a CSRF token.

response.body_schema: {"user": "<name>"}

description: Changes a user's password. Called by the UI server's change-password handler with X-Csrf-Token set from /auth/whoami. Passwords are always SHA-256 hex, never plaintext.

response.body_schema: empty output

description: Issues a new YT token for a user. Declared as method GET in the javascript-wrapper command table, so it never triggers the proxy's cookie-auth CSRF requirement. Used by the UI 'Manage tokens' dialog.

response.body_schema: the token string as a JSON/YSON scalar

description: Revokes a previously issued token by its SHA-256 hash.

response.body_schema: empty output

description: Lists a user's token hashes, optionally with metadata. Requires the user's password_sha256, which the UI obtains through the ManageTokens password modal (it re-validates the password by POSTing /api/yt/<cluster>/login first).

response.body_schema: list of sha256 hex strings, or {"<sha256>": <metadata yson>} when with_metadata is true

description: Batch command endpoint used by the UI server for cluster-params (with robot credentials) and by the browser for most page data. Not auth-specific, but a mock must serve it for any page to render.

headers.Authorization: OAuth <robot token> (server-side) or Cookie: YTCypressCookie=<value> (browser via the UI proxy)
headers.X-Csrf-Token: <csrf_token> - required by the proxy for cookie auth because this is a POST

response.body_schema: [{output?: any, error?: {code,message,attributes,inner_errors}}]

description: Plain-text proxy version. Called without credentials by getVersions and getClusterInfo. The cluster-info bootstrap only checks that the raw string is truthy; a missing or failed response makes the client render PRELOAD_ERROR.CONNECTION before it checks the auth result. getVersions separately extracts a semantic-looking version for the cluster menu.

response.body_schema: raw version string; getVersions matches it against /(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)/, while getClusterInfo returns it unchanged

description: Heavy-proxy discovery. The UI server calls it before forwarding any command whose javascript-wrapper descriptor has heavy:true, and uses res.data[0] as the target host. Skipped for local clusters or when disableHeavyProxies is set on the cluster config.

response.body_schema: ["host:port", ...]

description: Full proxy list, reachable from the browser only through the UI server's /api/yt-proxy/<cluster>/hosts-all whitelist. Used by the Components pages.

response.body_schema: [{name, role, banned, ...}]

description: Component versions, reachable through /api/yt-proxy/<cluster>/internal-discover_versions.

response.body_schema: {details: [{address, type, version, start_time, ...}], summary: {...}}

description: Proxy liveness. Returns 503 when the coordinator marks the proxy unavailable. Not used by the UI.

response.body_schema: empty; 503 ServiceUnavailable when the proxy is not available
